title: Millainen and minkälainen: describing one person or thing
focus: Millainen and minkälainen ask what one person or countable thing is like. Millainen talo on? — Talo on pieni.
targetSkills: Millainen and minkälainen: describing one person or thing

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “What is the house like?”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Millainen and minkälainen ask what one person or countable thing is like. They request a description, not its identity or name. These two question words are alternatives in the taught patterns. The complete question means “What is the house like”.
requiredSkills: Millainen and minkälainen: describing one person or thing
exercises.targetSkill: Millainen and minkälainen: describing one person or thing

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking for a description + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.role: question asking for a description
parts.formation: Millainen asks for the qualities of one person or countable thing.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Talo stays in its basic singular form here.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Millainen auto on?”: choose “The car is new.”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. An adjective is a word that describes a quality. Describe one countable thing with a basic-form adjective: Talo on pieni (“The house is small”). A short reply Pieni is natural too. The question and answer concern one whole person or thing; substance descriptions have their own later lesson. The complete reply means “The car is new”.
